about: How a line of text names the C# symbols it links to: words that name a type or member, words joined by dots that are the end of a symbol's qualified name as one symbol, and two words or more that are the end of a namespace's name as one namespace.
Cloyd's chat and the .NET Terminal Symbol Linker link names alike, and both are checked against these cases: Cloyd by Finding_the_symbols_a_line_names, the symbol linker by SymbolReferencesTest.

This file is the original, in ~/.claude at src/Cloyd.Specifications/Links/CasesSharedWithTheSymbolLinker. The symbol linker keeps a copy in its test resources, and its tests fail while the copy differs from it.
declarations: what each namespace declares, each type with its members' names and the types nested in it. A namespace without a name is the global one.
cases: each case's line, and the links it has, in order: each to a type or member, or to a namespace, covering its name from start, the line's first character being at 0.

cases.case: a type's member links as one symbol
a member qualified by its namespace links as one symbol
a type qualified by part of its namespace links as one symbol
a nested type's member links as one symbol
two names joined by a dot that are no type's member link each on its own
names before a type that are not its namespaces are left out of the link
a type with a member it doesn't have links as the type alone
a name of two letters links on its own
a name of one letter doesn't link on its own
a name of one letter links after its type's name
a namespace's name links as one namespace
the end of a namespace's name links as the namespace
a namespace with no types of its own links
one name of a namespace alone doesn't link
names of a namespace that leave out one between them don't link
a name in a path is part of the path
